ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, line $AB$ intersects line $CD$ at point $O$, $OE \perp CD$ and $OE$ bisects $\angle BOF$. If $\angle BOD$ is $10^\circ$ larger than $\angle BOE$, what is the degree measure of $\angle COF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}
Since $OE \perp CD$,\\
it follows that $\angle DOE = 90^\circ$,\\
which means $\angle DOB + \angle EOB = 90^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle DOB = \angle EOB + 10^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle EOB = 40^\circ$,\\
Since $OE$ bisects $\angle BOF$,\\
it follows that $\angle EOF = \angle BOE = 40^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $\angle COF = 90^\circ - \angle EOF = \boxed{50^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, line AB is a horizontal straight line, B is on the left side, A is on the right side, and point O is at the intersection point of the two lines. Line CD passes through O, C is at the upper right, and D is at the lower left, so OC and OD are opposite rays on the same straight line. Ray OE points from O to the upper left, and the problem states that OE ⟂ CD; ray OF points from O upward and slightly to the left, located between OC and OE. In the figure, OB is located inside the angle formed by OD and OE, and F is located inside the angle formed by OC and OE. Reasoning: Because OE ⟂ CD, and OD is on line CD, ∠DOE = 90°. Also because OB is located between OD and OE, ∠BOD + ∠BOE = 90°. Let ∠BOE = x; then the problem gives that ∠BOD is 10° greater than ∠BOE, namely ∠BOD = x + 10°. Thus x + (x + 10°) = 90°, solving gives 2x = 80°, so x = 40°, namely ∠BOE = 40°. OE bisects ∠BOF, so ∠EOF = ∠BOE = 40°. Also because OC is on line CD and OE ⟂ CD, ∠COE = 90°. In the figure, F is located between OC and OE, therefore ∠COF = ∠COE - ∠EOF = 90° - 40° = 50°.
